content.value:
A 30-second autonomous can't do everything. As time runs out, the robot needs to skip optional actions and just park.

Without time awareness, the robot blindly follows its fixed sequence and runs out of time mid-action.

TimerEx gives you methods to check remaining time and trigger different behaviors at the right moment.

new TimerEx(30) — a 30-second timer.

.start() — starts counting (safe to call multiple times, only starts once).

.getElapsed() — seconds since start.

.getRemaining() — seconds until duration ends.

.isDone() — true when timer hits 0.

.isMoreThan(seconds) — true when more than N seconds remain.

.isLessThan(seconds) — true when fewer than N seconds remain.

.restart() / .pause() / .resume()
Start the timer in initialize() and display the remaining time each tick with a RunCommand.

ConditionalCommand(onTrue, onFalse, condition) picks a branch each execution based on a BooleanSupplier.

Here, when more than 2 seconds remain, the full sequence runs. When time is short, a single parking message runs instead.

The condition is re-evaluated at schedule time — if the timer had more than 2 seconds at the start, the full sequence runs to completion even if time drops below 2 mid-sequence.

schedule(new ConditionalCommand(
    new SequentialCommandGroup(
        new InstantCommand(() -> telemetry.addData("Step", "Starting auto")),
        new WaitCommand(1000),
        new InstantCommand(() -> telemetry.addData("Step", "1 second passed")),
        new WaitCommand(1000),
        new InstantCommand(() -> telemetry.addData("Step", "2 seconds passed")),
        new WaitCommand(1000),
        new InstantCommand(() -> telemetry.addData("Step", "3 seconds passed")),
        new InstantCommand(() -> telemetry.addData("Step", "Auto finished"))
    ),
    new InstantCommand(() -> telemetry.addData("Step", "Skipping — parking instead")),
    () -> matchTime.isMoreThan(2)
));

The autonomous runs a 3-second sequence. Watch the "Time Remaining" count down from 30.

Since more than 2 seconds remain when the ConditionalCommand evaluates, the full sequence runs.

Notice: the condition is checked once at schedule time, not continuously. If you wanted continuous time-checking, you'd use a WaitUntilCommand inside the sequence instead.

content.question: What does isMoreThan(5) check?
options: If more than 5 seconds remain on the timer
If a command ran for more than 5 seconds
If the timer was paused for more than 5 seconds

content.question: ConditionalCommand evaluates its BooleanSupplier once when scheduled. True or false?
options: True — the branch is chosen at schedule time
False — it continuously re-evaluates every tick
